newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex assures petrochemical sale will boost output.
newsitem.headline: Pemex assures petrochemical sale will boost output.

text.p: Mexico's plan to partially privatize its state-owned petrochemical industry should boost national output, the head of state-owned oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos' (Pemex) petrochemical division said Monday.
Speaking at the 16th Latin American Petrochemical Industry conference, Luis Puig Lara estimated the division's 1996 petrochemical sales would total $1.62 million, with exports of $180 million.
He said the government is working to clarify its privatization strategy, which allows a minority stake in existing plants and full private ownership in new plants.
"Domestic and foreign competitiveness in this sector will feed off its own development and surely businesses soon to be developed will be a fundamental part of this new boost," Puig Lara said.
New businesses formed with Pemex will have long-term growth opportunities, he said.
The government changed its petrochemical sale plans two months ago, leaving many company executives wary and rethinking their interest in Mexico's plants.
